ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic Breast Cancer to the Uterus
Metastatic Colorectal Cancer to the Uterus

facts.raw_span: 54-year-old woman
history of stage III invasive ductal breast carcinoma
treated with mastectomy and chemoradiation 4 years earlier
urinary frequency
worsening right-sided pelvic pain
weight loss
MRI of the pelvis showed multiple fibroids and a heterogeneous 9.4 cm lesion involving the right uterine fundus/cornua
a detached, fragmented, ill-defined mass (14 × 12 × 4 cm) with fleshy solid and cystic components, central hemorrhage, and necrosis
the tumor invaded from the serosal surface into the myometrium

sheets of small, round hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, frequent mitoses (32 per 10 high-power fields), pseudo-rosette formation, foci of cytoplasmic clearing, and necrosis
diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1
negativity for keratin, DOG1, synaptophysin, desmin, myogenin, WT-1, CD45, inhibin, GATA-3, and SOX-10
